chapter_title: Concerning the Five Wonders that the Light Mind shall display in the Elect
chapter_note: This chapter is largely an institutional/ethical five-fold list aimed at the elect (preaching, faith, love, and especially legal excommunication). The only clear older teaching layer is the brief, impersonal cosmological-mechanical assertion that the Light Mind implants these five signs in the purified ‘new man’. The opening ‘apostle’ attribution is a compilation-frame marker; the closing beatitude and ‘faultless vessel/pearl’ rhetoric look like later moralizing rather than systematic cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: The Light Mind shall enact five light signs in the elect.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again the apostle speaks:” (hagiographic/compilation layer marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The clause about the Light Mind acting is cosmological/impersonal and could belong to the teaching core; the ‘Once again…the apostle speaks’ is a classic Kephalaia dialogue-frame seam that cannot be core.
Enumerated ‘first sign’ defined as preaching/proclaiming; institutional/paraenetic register about the elect’s activity rather than cosmological mechanism.
Second sign defined as faith produced in hearers after preaching; catechetical/community-oriented, not systematic cosmological exposition.
Third sign tied to ‘preaching’ and ‘assembly of his brethren’; even with lacunae, the social-ecclesial orientation is clear.
Fourth sign is ‘love’ directed to wisdom and to ‘brothers and sisters’ seated before him—community setting and moral virtue list.
Explicit church-discipline/institutional vocabulary (‘legal excommunication’, ‘church’) marks a later pastoral layer; this is not a cosmological five-fold degree map but governance.

paragraphs.core_text: The Light Mind puts these five signs in the new man, [whom he has] purified, cleansed, supported and chosen [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, process/mechanism language with a named Manichaean cosmic entity (Light Mind) acting upon the ‘new man’; this is the closest to the older teaching voice.
Beatitude-style exhortation (‘Blessed is every one…is diligent’) functions as moral encouragement rather than cosmological instruction.

Rhetorical closure praising perfection (‘faultless vessel’, ‘pearl without price’) reads as edifying/paraenetic and not part of a systematic cosmological scheme; the page marker and phrasing suggest an editorial conclusion.
